subject: Prefer CLI-first operator workflows and CMD success chaining

payload.summary: Software-engineering operations should prefer CLI/API/scripts over browser UI when reliable automation exists. When Windows CMD commands are strictly sequential and should stop on first failure, provide a single copy-pasteable chain using &&; reserve & for unconditional sequencing and | for stdout piping.

subject: Harden Windows CMD fail-fast chaining around batch gates

payload.summary: Observed that direct .cmd invocation inside an interactive && chain can allow later commands to run even when the batch script ends with a nonzero exit /b. The operator workflow rule is corrected: chained .cmd/.bat gates must be invoked with call, every gate must preserve a nonzero failure code, and longer critical flows should use an explicit orchestration script or fail-fast command block.

subject: Treat remote CI as asynchronous work

payload.summary: Remote CI should normally be dispatched and allowed to run asynchronously rather than mirrored into CMD with arbitrary sleeps or hand-written polling. Use a trustworthy blocking/streaming CLI primitive only when it has clear run identity and exit semantics; otherwise preserve exact branch/head/workflow identity and verify completion later before dependent merge or release actions.

subject: Promote repeated engineering orchestration into Qiven Operator

payload.summary: Stop extending ad-hoc CMD glue as the primary orchestration layer. Use a thin shell entrypoint over a reusable Python Operator owned by Devkit, with repository policy in small managed metadata. Python should own fail-fast process execution, dependency/parallel scheduling, human rendering, heartbeat/log buffering, real Git gates, machine-readable results, and asynchronous CI dispatch semantics.
